title: Dart import resolution: package: URIs not producing file-level edges
description: Sutra parses Arrow's Dart workspace (171 files, 574 symbols, 14k refs extracted) but 7,843 refs are unresolved — almost certainly the cross-package `package:arrow_*` imports. `sutra_deps` returns zero edges for any file, and the DD constraint engine reports "no import edges in workspace." This means forbidden_dep constraints (Arrow has 6 encoding its left-to-right package boundary) are dormant — they load correctly but never fire because no import graph exists to check against. Dart uses `package:foo/bar.dart` URIs that need to be resolved to workspace-relative file paths using the package's pubspec.yaml or .dart_tool/package_config.json. Arrow is a Dart monorepo with 4 packages (options, swe, core, calc) under one git repo, each with its own pubspec.yaml.

acceptance_criteria.text: package: URIs resolved to workspace-relative file paths
sutra_deps shows cross-package import edges for Arrow
forbidden_dep constraints fire on actual violations

execution_record: Parse of Arrow workspace: 5 packages discovered, 359 import edges resolved (was 0). Cross-package edges verified: calc→core(7), calc→options(15), core→options(21), core→swe(8), swe→options(6). No constraint violations found (Arrow's dependencies are clean — all edges flow right-to-left as intended). All 697 tests pass.

messages.author: codex
messages.text:
Codex adversarial review found 3 issues:

1. **[high, FIXED in b8a8428]** FK violation: delete_file_cascade would fail when resolved_file_id points to the deleted file. Fixed by NULLing resolved_file_id before delete.

2. **[high, accepted/deferred]** No backfill on NoChanges path — existing indexes won't get Dart edges until something changes. Accepted: sutra_add_root triggers full reparse, and adding work to the no-changes fast path defeats its purpose.

3. **[medium, accepted/deferred]** Pubspec renames don't invalidate resolved edges. Accepted: extremely rare, and delete_file_cascade now clears resolved_file_id so re-resolution happens naturally on next reparse cycle.
